text:
cs-erin: heads up — multiple customers reporting 502/503s from hosted API over the last 12m, customer-facing logs show worker restarts and some 401->503 spikes. noted high-retry counts. escalating. :rotating_light:
infra-ryan: thanks erin — can you paste one example request id and customer id? also any recent deploys?
cs-erin: req=78f3a1, cust=acme-inc. no platform deploys in last 2h, small canary rolled out to infra-minor yesterday but team said it's unrelated. customers seeing timeouts (~10s) then 503, sometimes 500. billing spikes for acme show duplicate tokens charged during retry loop.
eng-sam: grabbing logs from the upstream workers for req 78f3a1 now. initial glance: GPU OOM messages and then segfault in the inference runner.
eng-sam: paste from runner log: ```[2026-03-18T14:12:03Z] ERROR infer-runner: cudaErrorOutOfMemory: 2GB requested but only 1.8GB free
[2026-03-18T14:12:03Z] FATAL infer-runner: illegal instruction (SIGILL) at 0x7f2a...
[stacktrace trimmed]```. Seems like OOM leads to unstable state, container restarts, gateway returns 503.
maria-ml: interesting — is this happening only for long-context requests or also embeddings/batched small requests?
cs-erin: mostly long-chat sessions > 32k tokens and some toolcall-heavy flows. acme reported a user sending a 40k token doc + summarize -> timed out and retried.
eng-sam: I see dynbatch size spike in metrics for that GPU pool around the same time: queued tokens jumped, prefetch filled kv cache and memory ballooned. Also noticed a pattern where auth retries correlate: 401s from auth-proxy then client retries, which increases concurrency and pushes batch queues.
billing-zoe: acme noticed duplicate billing on their dashboard for ~12 requests during the incident window. can we confirm these were retries triggered by gateway 503s vs duplicate deliveries?
oncall-bot: incident-alert: upstream-gpu-pool-12 OOM rate 6 in 10m, restart_count > 3, fail_open:false, routed: hosted-api-gateway
infra-ryan: mitigation steps: 1) temporarily mark acme-inc in routing policy to throttle concurrency (per-customer limit) 2) disable kv-prefetch for hosted-api-gpu-pool-12 3) enable fallback to CPU-quantized model for their route (if applicable)
eng-sam: repro steps I'm trying (small script): ```# repro
for i in {1..100}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"large-chat-32k","input":"<40k tokens here>"}' &
done
wait
``` This floods dynbatch and triggers OOM on pool 12 in lab. Able to reproduce in staging with lower concurrency.
maria-ml: short-term guard: cap max_batch_tokens to 16k on pool-12 and set per-request max_context to 32k for hosted. Longer-term: add backpressure from auth-proxy on 401 spikes so we don't amplify retries into batch pressure.
billing-zoe: I'll pause manual billing adjustments but we should create a credit for acme and document duplicate charge cause. need root cause note.
cs-erin: customer update drafted: "We've identified upstream worker OOMs triggered by unexpectedly high concurrent large-context requests and amplified by auth retry loops. We've applied throttles and a fallback; we're investigating permanent fixes." sending after infra confirm.
eng-sam: root cause hypothesis: combination of (a) invalidated auth session causing clients to retry rapidly (401->re-auth->repeat), (b) request shapes (many large-context requests) causing dynbatch growth, (c) prefetch/kv cache filling causing memory ballooning -> cuda OOM -> segfault.
infra-ryan: actions and owners: - apply per-customer concurrency throttle (me) - disable kv-prefetch on pool-12 (me) - apply max_batch_tokens guard (maria) - create backpressure in auth-proxy to limit retry storm (eng-sam) - billing credit for acme (billing-zoe) - incident postmortem and runbook update (cs-erin)
eng-sam: rolling a hotfix in staging to cap batch token growth and add extra memory checks before allocating KV prefetch. will monitor for 15m.
oncall-bot: status-update: mitigation applied by infra-ryan at 14:28Z, error-rate decreased to baseline by 14:35Z.
cs-erin: customer notified, they acknowledged. opening postmortem ticket and scheduling follow-up with platform and auth teams.
eng-sam: follow-up tests to run: reproduce with auth proxy returning intermittent 401 + client retries, verify retries don't cause unbounded dynbatch growth. also add metrics: per-customer queued-token histogram.
maria-ml: flagging this for Optimize: recommend workload-specific quantization profile for large-context customers to reduce memory pressure.
cs-erin: thanks team. I'll close this channel once postmortem doc is up
